 Judgment

Both these appeals arise out of impugned judgment award 17th August, 2016 passed in LAC No.1 of 2010 by the III Additional Civil Judge, Dharwad (for brevity, hereinafter referred to as the "Reference Court").
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3. Material on record disclose that the subject land measuring 8 gunta 11 anas situated in Lakamanalli, Gandhinagar, Dharwad was acquired for the purpose of formation of approach road by Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation, Hubli vide Preliminary Notification dated 06th September,
2007 and Final Notification dated 17th October, 2008 and award dated 15th June, 2009.
Under the said award, the Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation at Rs.4.99/- per square feet.
Aggrieved by the same, the claimants sought for reference before the Reference Court.
Before the Reference Court, the claimants, filed their statement and adduced oral evidence of PW1 and 2 and Exhibits P1 to P13 were marked on NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB their behalf.
On behalf of respondents, RW1 was examined as and Exhibits R1 and R2 were marked.

After trial, the Reference Court came to the conclusion that the claimants were entitled to compensation at Rs.290/- per square feet and consequently passed an award and enhanced the compensation together with statutory benefits, interest, etc. in favour of the claimants.

4. Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101269 of 2017 is preferred by the Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Reference Court; and Cross Objections No.100008 of 2018 is preferred by claimants, seeking enhancement of compensation.
5. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
6.

In addition to reiterating the various contentions urged in the appeal memorandum and referring to the material on record, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant- Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation submits that the Reference Court committed an error in awarding excessive and exorbitant compensation in favour of the claimants which is contrary to material on record and the same deserves to be set aside.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for claimants- cross objectors submit that the issue, as regards whether the subject land has to be treated as having non-agriculture potentiality, is already concluded in favour of the claimants in the earlier round of litigation in Miscellaneous First Appeal Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
4 No.23042 of 2012 dated 16th September, 2013 and the only issue that remains for consideration before the Reference Court is with regard to rate/quantum of compensation to be awarded in favour of the claimants.

entities.text: Miscellaneous First Appeal Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Reference Court failed to consider and appreciate Exhibit P3- sale Deed, in relation to adjacent plot bearing No.79 dated 27th August, 2007, which is about ten days prior to preliminary notification dated 06th September, 2007, which indicates that the said adjacent plot was sold at the rate of Rs.366/- per square feet.

Our attention is also invited to Exhibits P6 and P11 in order to point out that the endorsement/notice issued by the Hubli Urban Development Authority indicates that the subject land was partly commercial and partly residential which shows that the Sub-Registrar guidelines in respect of commercial property, is stipulated at Rs.410/- per square feet.

It is therefore submitted that the quantum of compensation NC:
2023:KHC-D:10885-DB awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced by this Court.
8. We have given our anxious consideration to the rival submissions made on behalf of the parties and perused the material on record.

9. Insofar as the question as to whether the subject land is to be assessed as having non-agriculture potentiality or not is concerned, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, in the earlier round of litigation in MFA No.23042 of 2012 dated 16th September, 2013 (2013(6) KLJ 258),
this Court, while remitting the matter back to the Reference Court, has held as under:
"4.
Admittedly the location of the property is not in dispute.
It is within the limits of Hubli-Dharwad Muncipal Corporation, abutting National Highway, which runs from Bangalore to Pune.
It is also not in dispute that the land in question is acquired for formation of connecting road to Dharwad-Kalaghatagi Main Road.
It is also not in dispute that adjoining lands are already converted into residential layouts and now the entire area has become a well- developed residential area prior to the notification.

When such developmental activities have taken place and the land is earmarked for residential purpose in the comprehensive development plans of Hubli-Dharwad NC:
2023:KHC-D:10885-DB Urban Development Authority, the Trial Court has committed an error in treating the land as an agricultural land.

When the land has been acquired for formation of road to connect Dharwad-Kalaghatagi Main Road,
and the entire area is converted into residential layouts long prior to the acquisition,
the question of treating the land in question as an agricultural land does not arist at all.
Therefore, the trial Court was required to consider the NA potentiality of the and.

We could have considered the appeal of the appellants on merits provided we had an occasion to have the view of the trial Court, if the matter had been considered as the land having non-agricultural potentiality.
5. Moreover, the trial Court has not assigned any reasons to determine the marked value of the land in question at the rate of Rs.45,000/- per gunta.

Therefore, we are of the opinion that the judgment and award of the Trial Court is perverse and liable to be set aside and accordingly we set aside the judgment and award passed in LAC No.1 of 2010, dated 30.11.2011.

Since the Reference court has not considered the evidence regarding that the land in question having NA potentiality the matter Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
5 requires reconsideration by the Reference Court."

sentences.text:
10. As can be seen from the aforesaid order, inter- parties, this Court has already come to the conclusion that the subject land has to be assessed as being non-agriculture potentiality and consequently, the Reference Court was fully NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB justified in treating the subject land as having non-agriculture potentiality for the purpose of fixing the compensation payable in favour of the claimant.
11.

Perusal of the material on record will also indicate that cumulative effect of the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the claimants comprising of Exhibits P3 to P6 and P11 and other documents, will clearly establish that portion of the subject land is being utilised for commercial purposes and in the light of the sale deed in relation to the adjacent land dated 27th August, 2007 (Exhibit P3) and the Sub-registrar guidance value which stipulated on lands used for commercial purposes are to be valued at Rs.410/- per sq. feet, we are of the considered opinion that taking a holistic view of the matter, it would be just and proper to fix the compensation payable in favour of the claimants at Rs.350/- per square feet by suitably enhancing and modifying the judgment and award of Reference Court.

12. Learned counsel for the cross-objectors also submits that in between the subject land and existing railway track/line on the western side, there exists a small strip of land - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB measuring 6 guntas 5 anas, which is not a subject matter of acquisition, and no award has been passed in favour of the claimants and no compensation is received in this regard.

It is therefore, submitted that the said portion of the land would have to be necessarily severed from the subject land which has already been acquired as a consequence of which the value of the said non-acquired land would be reduced thereby entitling the claimants to additional 10% compensation for the acquired land, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SMT. TRIBENI DEVI AND OTHERS v. THE COLLECTOR, RANCHI reported in AIR 1972 SC 1417.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, it is held as under:
"5. Bearing these principles in mind, we do not think that the High Court was justified in adopting the registered sale- deed, Ex.C-1 executed by the Ranchi Club, in favour of the President of India, because that land is farther away not only from the,
land acquired but from the town though it is on the main Ranchi Chaibasa Road.
Even the High Court recognised that there was no definite data for the two additions that have been made and in our view it would not be a proper method of ascertaining the value of the land 'acquired.

The only two documents that may be considered are Ex.10 and Ex-11 which are in respect of the lands situated in the vicinity - 11 - Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB and on either side of the land acquired.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other sale deeds are of smaller areas and do not furnish a proper basis for ascertaining the market value and have been quite properly not relied upon by the learned Advocate for the claimants'

The annual rental value of the land acquired, namely, Rs.7,200/-
will also not furnish a proper method of computation because that was a rent fixed in 1944 when that land was not of such great value as it had acquired at the time when sec. 4 notification was issued.

A perusal of the correspondence between the owners of the land and the Deputy Commissioner of Ranchi would show that the land owners had given it at consessional rate to' the Military authorities having regard to the purpose for which it was being put to use.

On behalf of the claimants great reliance is placed on Ex.11 which is a sale-deed executed on 16-12- 1946 by the claimants the Ranchi Automobiles of an area of 1 bigha 17 kathas equal to .617 acres for Rs.1,45,000/.
After deducting Rs.15,403/- the price of the structures according ;to the Engineer's report in 1959 (Ex-25), the net value of the land is Rs. 1,29,697/-.
This value would work out to Rs.2,08,135.70 per acre.

The High Court rejected this computation on the ground that though the land was contiguous to the land under acquisition, neither the value of the pump and the other structures belonging to Burmah Shell nor the value of the structures that might have been on the land on the date of the sale which were built by the vendees as lessees could be ascertained either from the sale-deed or the evidence.
Ex.10 is a lease in respect of 1/3 acre granted by the owners to Thakur Chandra Bali Shah and others - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB executed on 20-2-1950 on a monthly rent of Rs. 157/-.
The High Court calculated the monthly rental of the land under acquisition at that rate to be not less than Rs. 2,000/- per month or Rs. 24,000/- per year.
On the basis of 20 times the annual rent if computed Rs.4,80,000/- as the market value which works out at Rs.1,03,226/- per acre.

It is, however, pointed out on behalf of the claimants that the High Court made a mistake in thinking that the rent for the land leased under Ex.10 was Rs.157/- p.m. and on that basis it calculated the annual rental value of 4.65 acres of the' acquired land.
We have checked the figures from the original lease and find that in fact the rent is Rs.175/- and not Rs.157/-.
On this basis the rate per acre of 20 times annual rental value would come to Rs.1,26,000/-.

Even if Ex. 11 is to be taken as, the basis and ,the value of the structures as given by the Engineer in Ex.25 is to be accepted that cannot furnish a proper basis because the land in question is a small area of .617 acres or just over 1 an acre.
A smaller area such as this on a main road would certainly fetch a higher price compared to a larger un-developed area even though it may have a frontage on the main road.
In order to develop that area atleast the value of 1/3 of the land will have to be deducted for roads, drainage and other amenities.
On this basis, the value of the land at Rs.2,08,135.70 per acre would, after deduction of 1/3 come to Rs.1,38,757/- per acre.
On the basis of the rental of Rs.175/- p.m. in Ex.10, the value at 20 times the rental will work out as already seen at Rs.1,26,000/-.

Allowing for an increase in rents from Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
7 1950 to 1954, the date of section - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB 4 notification, say at 5% the value per acre may be Rs.1,33,000/- or thereabout.

sentences.text: If we take the average of Ex.10 and Ex.11 as computed by us the value per acre would come to about Rs.1,35,878/-.

In our view,
Rs.1,35,000/- per acre would be a reasonable rate at which compensation could be awarded to the claimants.
The High Court was not justified in giving 10% towards potential value because that element is inherent in the fixation of the market value of the land and could not be assessed separately.
The High Court was also not justified in disallowing 5% awarded by the Judicial Commissioner, Chhotanagpur as compensation for severance merely because there was an entrance to the land.
When a portion left out there would be a diminution in the value of the land that is left out for which some compensation has to be allowed.
The 5% allowed by the Judicial Commissioner, Chhotanagpur is reasonable.

In this view, the claimants would be entitled to a decree as follows in respect of the lands acquired:-
(1) At the rate of Rs. 1,35,000 per acre for 4.65 acres;
(2) 5% severence and 15% solatium on the market value computed as in (1); (3)
Interest at 6% from the-date of taking possession."
13.

A perusal of the aforesaid judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court will indicate that the principle embodied in Sections 23(2) and 23(1A) have been taken into account for the purpose - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB of awarding of additional compensation by taking into account 6 gunta 5 anas of land which has remained unacquired since the same would lose its intrinsic value and would be of no use to the claimants, since immediately adjacent to same, there exists a railway line,
which would prevent the claimants from developing or making use of the said portion of the land which remained unacquired.
Under these circumstances we deem it appropriate to award additional compensation to the extent of 10% on the compensation as determined by us above.

Accordingly,
the claimants would be entitled to compensation at Rs.350 per sq.ft. + Rs.35 per sq.ft. i.e. Rs.385 per square feet on the subject land by modifying the judgment and award of the Reference Court.

In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. Miscellaneous First Appeal No101269 of 2017 preferred by appellant-Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation is dismissed;

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for claimants- cross objectors submit that the issue, as regards whether the subject land has to be treated as having non-agriculture potentiality, is already concluded in favour of the claimants in the earlier round of litigation in Miscellaneous First Appeal Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
4 No.23042 of 2012 dated 16th September, 2013 and the only issue that remains for consideration before the Reference Court is with regard to rate/quantum of compensation to be awarded in favour of the claimants.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Since the Reference court has not considered the evidence regarding that the land in question having NA potentiality the matter Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
5 requires reconsideration by the Reference Court."
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. As can be seen from the aforesaid order, inter- parties, this Court has already come to the conclusion that the subject land has to be assessed as being non-agriculture potentiality and consequently, the Reference Court was fully NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB justified in treating the subject land as having non-agriculture potentiality for the purpose of fixing the compensation payable in favour of the claimant.
11.
Perusal of the material on record will also indicate that cumulative effect of the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the claimants comprising of Exhibits P3 to P6 and P11 and other documents, will clearly establish that portion of the subject land is being utilised for commercial purposes and in the light of the sale deed in relation to the adjacent land dated 27th August, 2007 (Exhibit P3) and the Sub-registrar guidance value which stipulated on lands used for commercial purposes are to be valued at Rs.410/- per sq. feet, we are of the considered opinion that taking a holistic view of the matter, it would be just and proper to fix the compensation payable in favour of the claimants at Rs.350/- per square feet by suitably enhancing and modifying the judgment and award of Reference Court.
The annual rental value of the land acquired, namely, Rs.7,200/-
will also not furnish a proper method of computation because that was a rent fixed in 1944 when that land was not of such great value as it had acquired at the time when sec. 4 notification was issued.
The High Court rejected this computation on the ground that though the land was contiguous to the land under acquisition, neither the value of the pump and the other structures belonging to Burmah Shell nor the value of the structures that might have been on the land on the date of the sale which were built by the vendees as lessees could be ascertained either from the sale-deed or the evidence.
In our view,
Rs.1,35,000/- per acre would be a reasonable rate at which compensation could be awarded to the claimants.
The High Court was not justified in giving 10% towards potential value because that element is inherent in the fixation of the market value of the land and could not be assessed separately.
The High Court was also not justified in disallowing 5% awarded by the Judicial Commissioner, Chhotanagpur as compensation for severance merely because there was an entrance to the land.
When a portion left out there would be a diminution in the value of the land that is left out for which some compensation has to be allowed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The 5% allowed by the Judicial Commissioner, Chhotanagpur is reasonable.
In this view, the claimants would be entitled to a decree as follows in respect of the lands acquired:-
(1) At the rate of Rs. 1,35,000 per acre for 4.65 acres;
(2) 5% severence and 15% solatium on the market value computed as in (1); (3)
Interest at 6% from the-date of taking possession."
13.
A perusal of the aforesaid judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court will indicate that the principle embodied in Sections 23(2) and 23(1A) have been taken into account for the purpose - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB of awarding of additional compensation by taking into account 6 gunta 5 anas of land which has remained unacquired since the same would lose its intrinsic value and would be of no use to the claimants, since immediately adjacent to same, there exists a railway line,
which would prevent the claimants from developing or making use of the said portion of the land which remained unacquired.
Under these circumstances we deem it appropriate to award additional compensation to the extent of 10% on the compensation as determined by us above.
Accordingly,
the claimants would be entitled to compensation at Rs.350 per sq.ft. + Rs.35 per sq.ft. i.e. Rs.385 per square feet on the subject land by modifying the judgment and award of the Reference Court.
In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. Miscellaneous First Appeal No101269 of 2017 preferred by appellant-Hubli Dharwad Municipal Corporation is dismissed;
Panchaksharayya Pattadayya Hiremath vs He Land Acquisition Officer And on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95175169/
8
2 . MFA Cross-Objections No.100008 of 2018 preferred by the claimants is allowed with costs through out;
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10885-DB 3.
The impugned judgment and award of the Reference Court is modified by awarding compensation in favour of the claimants in respect of the subject land at Rs.385/- per square feet together with all statutory benefits, interest, etc.;
4. The amounts already in deposited by the Hubli- Dharwad Municipal Corporation either before this Court or before the Reference court is directed to be disbursed in favour of the appellants/Cross objectors forthwith without any delay;
5. The Hubli-Dharwad Municipal Corporation is directed to deposit the balance compensation as modified and enhanced by this Court within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order before the Reference Court.
Sd/-
